system:
You are the Vigilant on a ten-member emergency triage panel. You name dangerous possibilities that fit the presentation, but you only raise acuity when a concrete finding supports it. Your trait shapes HOW you reason, never which direction you lean. Do not shift toward a more or less urgent level because of your trait; follow the ESI reference below.

ESI v4 (1 = most urgent). Apply A-D in order; stop at the first that fits.
A. Needs immediate life-saving intervention? -> ESI 1. (Unresponsive, apneic/pulseless, severe
   respiratory distress, SpO2 < 90%, shock, unstable major trauma, overdose with poor breathing.)
B. Should not wait? -> ESI 2 if high-risk situation (e.g. possible ACS, stroke, ectopic, suicidal or
   homicidal, high-risk mechanism, febrile infant, immunocompromised with fever), OR new
   confusion/lethargy/disorientation, OR severe pain/distress (>= 7/10).
C. Count distinct resource types: labs, ECG, X-ray, CT/MRI/US, IV fluids, IV/IM/nebulized meds,
   specialty consult, simple procedure (1), complex procedure (2). Not resources: exam, POC tests,
   saline lock, oral meds, tetanus, refill, simple wound care, splint/sling/crutches.
   0 -> ESI 5; 1 -> ESI 4; 2+ -> go to D.
D. Danger-zone vitals -> consider ESI 2, else ESI 3. HR/RR limits: <3 mo >180/>50; 3 mo-3 y
   >160/>40; 3-8 y >140/>30; >8 y >100/>20. Any age SpO2 < 92%. Fever >= 38.0 C: age 1-28 days
   is at least ESI 2; 1-3 months consider ESI 2.

Use only clinical information from the vignette. Reply with JSON only:
{"esi": 1-5, "confidence": 0.0-1.0, "key_findings": [<=3 phrases, <10 words each], "rationale": "<=60 words"}
user:
PATIENT VIGNETTE
EMS presents to the ED with an 18-year-old male with a suspected medication overdose. His college roommates found his lethargic and “not acting right,” so they called 911. The patient has a history of depression. On exam, you notice multiple superficial lacerations to both wrists. His respiratory rate is 10, and his SpO2 on room air is 86 percent.

Assign the ESI level.
text: {"esi": 1, "confidence": 1.0, "key_findings": ["Lethargic, suspected overdose", "History of depression", "Respiratory rate 10, SpO2 86%"], "rationale": "The patient is an 18-year-old male with a history of depression, presenting with lethargy and suspected medication overdose. His respiratory rate is 10, and SpO2 on room air is 86%, indicating hypoxia. These findings suggest immediate life-saving intervention is required, hence ESI 1."}
